metadata.data_sources: IMO Polar Code Guidelines, NSIDC Sea Ice Index, NOAA OSCAR Ocean Currents, IHO/IOC GEBCO Bathymetry, Indian Antarctic Programme historical expedition logs

end.name: Maitri Research Station, Antarctica
end.shelf_fast_ice_landing: Lazarev Ice Shelf / Princess Astrid Coast

voyage_info.ice_conditions: Favorable - minimum seasonal ice extent, open leads along 10-15°E meridian
voyage_info.weather_window_requirement: 72-hour calm weather window (<20 kts wind) required before entering pack ice at 64°S

maritime_constraints.vessel_polar_class: 1A Ice Class (DNV ICE-1A / Polar Class 6 equivalent)

routes.name: Eastern Ice-Avoidance Route
routes.description: Maximum ice avoidance route. Wide eastern detour around Iceberg Alley (40-60°E) and Prince Edward Islands. Lowest collision probability.
key_features: Passes wide east of Prince Edward Islands (46.7°S, 37.8°E)
Wide 350 km berth clear of main iceberg concentration corridor (40-60°E)
Gradual southern descent through the Roaring Forties and Furious Fifties
Enters pack ice at 66°S where ice concentration is lowest (<30%)

routes.name: Direct Southern Route
routes.description: Most direct orthodromic route. Transits straight across the 40-50°E sector through Iceberg Alley. Saves 6 days but increases ice hazard exposure.
key_features: Near Great Circle route from South of India directly to Queen Maud Land
Cuts overall transit time to 28 days

waypoints.label: Roaring Forties Direct Gate
waypoints.notes: High swell encounters; watch for rogue waves

waypoints.label: West of Prince Edward Fracture Zone
waypoints.notes: Deep trench clearance between Prince Edward and Crozet

waypoints.label: Iceberg Alley TRANSIT CORRIDOR
waypoints.notes: High iceberg density; daylight lookouts mandatory

waypoints.label: Dense Pack Ice Lead Navigation
waypoints.notes: Ice speed reduced to 8 kts; searchlight navigation

waypoints.label: Maitri Station Fast-Ice Anchorage - ARRIVAL
waypoints.notes: Direct arrival at fast ice mooring point

routes.name: Current-Assisted Western Route
routes.description: Exploits favorable Southern Ocean currents (Antarctic Circumpolar Current eddies & Agulhas Return flow) to minimize engine load and fuel burn.
key_features: Rides favorable ocean current vectors between 35°S and 48°S
Saves 33,000 liters of marine diesel fuel compared to eastern route
Avoids shallow bank of Prince Edward Islands via western flank
Moderate ice exposure at 64°S with favorable drift

wind_regimes.roaring_forties: 40-50°S, prevailing Westerlies 25-35 kts with frequent storm gales
wind_regimes.furious_fifties: 50-60°S, persistent Westerlies 30-45 kts, significant wave height 6-10m
wind_regimes.coastal_katabatic_winds: 68-71°S, off Antarctic plateau, intermittent gusts exceeding 50 kts

ice_concentration_by_latitude.60_to_64_south: 10 - 25% (marginal ice zone, loose brash and bergy bits)
ice_concentration_by_latitude.64_to_68_south: 30 - 60% (medium first-year pack ice with open leads)
ice_concentration_by_latitude.68_to_71_south: 70 - 90% (heavy fast ice barrier along Queen Maud Land)

hazards.name: Iceberg Alley (Weddell/Enderby Drift Corridor)
hazards.notes: Large tabular bergs calving from Amery and Riiser-Larsen shelves drifting northwest

hazards.name: Prince Edward Islands Sub-Antarctic Shallows
hazards.notes: Isolated rocky shelves, localized magnetic anomalies, sudden dense fog

hazards.name: Bouvet Island Remote Hazard
hazards.notes: Uninhabited volcanic island with heavy wave surges and grounding icebergs

hazards.name: Riiser-Larsen / Lazarev Ice Shelf Calving Margin
hazards.notes: Fast ice breakup zone and potential multi-year pressure ridges
